neg rax
mov r10,rdi

3859b139b5.why: Compute the wrapping 32-bit scaled index directly in eax, then negate rax after updating rdx. Since r8 is dead, this removes the copy into rax while preserving the zero extension before the 64-bit negation.

8a0b896f43.why: The two loads, two packed additions, packing, clamps with arbitrary incoming bounds, store, and live pointer updates have no removable instruction at SSE4.1.

1aaa686ad1.why: All three address updates are live, and producing the negative logical half of the original rdx still requires both the shift and negation.

6a4fa9ac10.why: SSE2 needs both byte unpacks and a copy to retain their shared input, while the potentially unaligned second load cannot safely be folded into legacy unpack memory operands.

90d9f8b0e8.why: All three address updates are live, and producing the negative logical half of the original rdx still requires both the shift and negation.

55ea17f348.why: All three initialized vector registers and both updated scalar registers are live, with one instruction already used for each result.

0fc0b8a452.why: The four byte-prefix stages require their copies, shifts, and additions under SSSE3, and the addition into xmm2, store, shuffle, and index update are all observable.

933bb295e1.why: The AVX sequence already folds the load into the XOR and uses three-operand shifts and additions, leaving no redundant prefix stage, store, shuffle, or index update.

e12ef4b9dc.why: Each of the three live vector results needs its own initialization, including zeroing the upper halves of ymm1 and ymm2, and both scalar updates are live.

d3a6c0a934.why: The lane-local prefix sums, additions into xmm2, cross-lane extraction, two stores, arbitrary-mask shuffles, and final index update are all required.

3ed914ebe5.why: Every zeroed register and the rcx-to-r9 copy is live, and SSE4.1 provides no instruction to initialize these independent destinations together.

498611eb5f.why: The arbitrary 32-bit products and live accumulators need the broadcast, multiplies, and additions, while potentially unaligned sample loads prevent safe folding into legacy PMULLD memory operands.

ad17123bd2.why: The three shifted accumulators remain live, and each residual requires its load, subtraction, and store in addition to the live scalar updates.

06fdaaa96e.why: Both products and accumulations, both loads into live vector registers, and the flag-setting index increment are necessary.

e39834e43f.why: The updated xmm2 and full final xmm0 value must be retained, so a scalar memory add cannot replace the load-add-store sequence.

bb621774d6.why: Although xmm1 is dead, replacing the final three SIMD instructions with an extract and scalar memory add would clobber the required incoming flags.

258e74c7c6.why: The full shifted xmm2 and final xmm0 values are live, preventing a scalar-only replacement of the final load-add-store sequence.

3ea04f704c.why: Although xmm1 is dead, replacing the final three SIMD instructions with an extract and scalar memory add would clobber the required incoming flags.

54907085ff.why: The wrapping 32-bit scale, 64-bit pointer addition and negation, and live xmm4 initialization each require an instruction.

6daf857321.why: SSE2 requires a load, packed shift, and store for each 128-bit chunk, and the index update must also reproduce SF and OF.
